perspective:
Brandon Talayumptewa’s available information is limited to what he personally experiences, observes, hears, says, and thinks in his interactions with Benjamin:

- He is an insurance agent meeting Benjamin Erickson, an entrepreneur, professionally for business insurance advice.
- He is aware Benjamin has limited formal education and worries about explaining complex insurance terms clearly.
- In their first meeting, he hears Benjamin want comprehensive coverage and admit some terms are new. Brandon explains liability insurance as a safety net and asset protection as a guard over inventory/equipment. He hears Benjamin ask for an example, then say the explanation makes sense and thanks him.
- In a later meeting, Brandon has revised his view of Benjamin’s ability to understand details; he feels more confident and plans to discuss more complex policy options. He hears Benjamin say he is ready and has been reading up. Brandon explains business interruption and property/theft coverage; he hears Benjamin call these points crucial and reassuring.
- At a casual lunch, Brandon feels insecure about being seen as too detail-oriented/cautious and tries to balance thoroughness with engaging conversation. He hears Benjamin appreciate his thoroughness and enjoy lighter moments. Brandon tells a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds; he hears Benjamin react with fascination and comment on the stakes. Brandon connects it to risk assessment for Benjamin’s business; Benjamin agrees it is less unusual but equally important.
- After Benjamin’s positive response, Brandon feels pleased and decides to offer additional support beyond insurance. He tells Benjamin he wants to add value and suggests strategic investments, such as security upgrades, could protect assets and lower premiums. He hears Benjamin call his insights invaluable, agree it is smart/win-win, and want to explore further.
- Encouraged by their successful collaboration, Brandon feels optimistic and proposes a joint venture: co-developing a platform integrating risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. He hears Benjamin agree, call the idea groundbreaking, say combining their expertise could set them apart, and suggest drafting initial plans.
